body: Our house has a box room, full of boxes that we still haven't unpacked from our last move. A couple of weeks ago something in that room started intermittently beeping . It's not necessarily slop, but it reads like slop! It's very easy to spot an AI-written PR, and as with other forms of AI writing my instant reaction is best summarized as "I'm not reading all of that". Monitors your RAM and reports any "quite terrible" unused capacity directly to the CEO of OpenAI.

README 節錄：# Ram-Altman **A bash script that writes to Sam Altman once a day to report the RAM he missed.** Read the sample emails at **ram-altman.lol**, no install needed. There is RAM in your computer. Right now. Just sitting there, in a *personal* computer, being personal. You may have thought of this as "a computer working normally". On a recent episode of Cheeky Pint, the CEO of OpenAI offered another view: > "From a global allocation perspective, actually, it's quite terrible to have everybody have a bunch of the world's limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer" > > — Sam Altman That RAM, he added, is "being used maybe 5% of the time". Which raised an obvious question for a certain kind of person: *surely someone should be monitoring this?* So we wrote a script. If your machine has more than 10% of its RAM available, it sends one email a day to let Sam know. It seemed only fair. He can't fix the problem if nobody tells him where the RAM is. ## Features - Tracks total, used and available RAM, plus your standing with the global allocation authorities - Handles page cache correctly, which already puts it ahead of most arguments about RAM - Sends at most one email per day, because we're hoarders, not animals - Rotates 8 subject lines, 10 messages and 6 sign-offs, so the joke gets old at a carefully managed pace - Logs every sample to CSV for when the auditors arrive
